whatPmDoes.root: A PM decides what a product should do, and why.
whatPmDoes.sub: Not: managing people, writing code, or designing screens.

constraints.note: Every call has to satisfy all three at once. Drop one and the product fails.

flow.detail: Talk to users. Watch them use the product. Read support tickets. The skill is separating what people say from what they do — usually different.
Say no to good ideas so the great ones get built. Use a framework — RICE, or impact vs effort — to make the trade-off visible, and tie every call to a goal.
One page: what to build, who it's for, what success looks like, what's out of scope. An engineer should be able to question and estimate it without a meeting.
Release gradually — 5% of users first. Watch the dashboard. Then the real question: did the metric actually move, or did something else change at the same time?
Tell stakeholders what's happening before it goes wrong. A slipped date is manageable; a surprise slipped date is a crisis. Never blindside your manager.
